 Renaissance Technologies Sold 99.7% Of Its $1.42 Billion Nvidia Stake Before Jensen Huang’s Exit, While Building A $1.62 Billion Stake In Another Chip Stock

 Renaissance Technologies dumped 99.7% of its Nvidia shares in the third quarter while piling into Micron, a stake now worth about $1.62 billion. 
 The filing surfaced the same day Jensen Huang resigned, but the Sept. 30 snapshot suggests coincidence, since nothing indicates Renaissance knew in advance. 
 Renaissance cut Taiwan Semiconductor and Broadcom while adding Sandisk and Lam Research, shifting from AI chip leaders toward memory and equipment names.

 Renaissance Technologies, the quantitative firm founded by the late Jim Simons, all but left NVIDIA ( NASDAQ:NVDA ) in the third quarter. Its 13F filing for the quarter ended Sept. 30, 2026 shows 23,170 NVIDIA shares worth $5,327,269, after the firm cut 7,068,086 shares during the quarter. Matthew Kerr of Quiver Quantitative reported the stake fell from 7.09 million shares, and TheStreet put the reduction at 99.7%. TheStreet, citing WhaleWisdom, estimated the position at $1.42 billion at the June 30 close. That figure reflects the stake's value on that date. The filing does not show when Renaissance sold or what it received. 
 vzphotos / iStock Editorial via Getty Images A Striking Date That Appears to Be Coincidence 
 The filing became public Nov. 12, 2026, the same day NVIDIA announced Jensen Huang's resignation and named CFO Colette Kress interim chief executive. As far as anyone knows, the timing was a coincidence. A 13F is a Sept. 30 record taken weeks before the announcement, the exact sale dates within the quarter are unknown, and nothing suggests Renaissance knew anything in advance. Renaissance is a quant fund that trades a very large number of positions, and a 13F gives no reasons, so no single move represents a stated view. 
 NVIDIA closed at $162.85 on Nov. 13, down 26.41% over the past month. Bloomberg reported Sunday on a possible Huang comeback, adding another variable for shareholders.

 Micron Is the Other Chip Stock 
 Renaissance held 1,520,639 shares of Micron Technology ( NASDAQ:MU ) worth $1,619,650,963 at Sept. 30, after adding 1,309,059 shares. Matthew Kerr of Quiver Quantitative rounded that value to $1.62 billion and put the share-count increase at 619%. TheStreet put the June count at 211,580 shares and said Micron was up 180% for the year through Nov. 12. 
 Micron closed at $778.31 on Nov. 13, up 172.91% year to date but down 14.86% over the past month. Fiscal fourth-quarter revenue reached $54.229 billion, up 379.27%, with a non-GAAP gross margin of 87.0%. Management forecast to $61.5 billion in fiscal first-quarter revenue and non-GAAP EPS of $38.15. Chief operating officer Manish Bhatia said Micron has "more than 75% of our shipments committed for the year." 
 AMD Was the Second Big Chip Addition 
 Renaissance held 1,995,101 shares of Advanced Micro Devices ( NASDAQ:AMD ) worth $1,205,536,416, after adding 1,165,404 shares. Matthew Kerr of Quiver Quantitative put the increase at 140%. AMD's third-quarter Data Center revenue rose 97% to $8.546 billion, and it forecast fourth-quarter revenue to about $17 billion. Shares closed at $534.06, up 149.37% year to date. 
 Chip Leaders Out, Memory and Equipment In 
 The same filing shows Renaissance cut Taiwan Semiconductor to 126,320 shares, cut Broadcom to 734 shares and left Marvell. It added Sandisk and Lam Research and opened a new 305,332-share position in the VanEck Semiconductor ETF, whose largest holding is Nvidia. The pattern leans away from AI chip leaders toward memory and chip-equipment names, and the filing offers no reason (we reverse-engineered what the first signals of the biggest chip winners looked like in a free Next Nvidia playbook). 
 Big Tech Exits and a New SpaceX Stake 
 Renaissance opened a SpaceX position of 4,113,200 shares worth $620,517,529. It held 1,577 Meta shares, down from 2.02 million according to Matthew Kerr of Quiver Quantitative. Seeking Alpha reported Apple fell to 3,246 shares from 1.59 million, and Seeking Alpha put Amazon at 11,128 shares, down from 2.29 million. New positions in Goldman Sachs and Bank of America also appeared. 
 What This Filing Can Tell You Before NVIDIA Reports 
 A 13F is a quarter-end record, filed weeks later, with no reasons attached. Renaissance may have changed these positions since Sept. 30, and the NVIDIA timing appears to be a coincidence. The more useful signal for investors lies in the companies' own numbers. 
 NVIDIA is expected to report fiscal third-quarter results after the close on Nov. 17, against guidance of $108B ±2% in revenue. In August, Kress said, "We expect supply to remain a bottleneck at least through the end of fiscal year '28." Watch whether the company meets that guidance and what the interim leadership says about demand, memory costs and taking over.
